facts.value: € 950/month median room rent (Kamernet, Q2 2026; +0.5% y/y) - most expensive Dutch city
facts.notes: Kamernet median rent for rooms (max 30 m2) advertised on Kamernet by private landlords/tenants/agencies; social student housing excluded. Advertised asking rents, not what existing tenants pay. The Q2 2026 figures were read on a rolling URL that is overwritten by each new quarterly report. UvA budgets € 650-1,200/month for accommodation and says finding housing can be very challenging.

facts.value: Not found on an official/citable source

UvA items: accommodation 650-1,200, living 400-500, insurance 35-100, books 50-100. VU cites Nibud: about € 1,400/month (national). No academic year stated.

facts.value: Temperate maritime: avg 3.8 °C in Jan, 18.1 °C in Jul; ~850 mm rain/yr; ~1780 h sun/yr (KNMI 1991-2020, Schiphol)
Very international city; student and study associations, University Sports Centre, CREA culture centre; museums, music, festivals.
facts.source_name: University of Amsterdam - living in Amsterdam

facts.value: No Dutch needed for English-taught programmes; English is widely spoken. Dutch helps for part-time jobs/internships and is sometimes required.
facts.notes: National source, applies to the whole country. UvA: English widely spoken in Amsterdam; learning Dutch 'can help you feel at home'.

facts.value: Hospitality is the most common student job; also TA posts and VU's student-job board. Non-EU: max 16 h/week, or full-time Jun-Aug.
facts.source_name: VU Amsterdam - cost of living and working

facts.value: Statutory minimum from 1 Jul 2026: € 14.99/h gross at 21+; € 11.99 (age 20), € 8.99 (19), € 7.50 (18). Same nationwide.
facts.notes: Legal floor, not a measured 'typical' student wage for this city; many student jobs pay at or near this minimum. Rates from 1 Jan 2026 were € 14.71 (21+).
